chunks: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'The Hand of God is above the head of the ruler, hovering with mercy. So when he acts unjustly, God leaves him to himself.'

key_terms.الْحَاكِمِ: The ruler/judge — one in authority, whether a political leader or a judicial officer
key_terms.تُرَفْرِفُ: Hovers/flutters — evocative image of a protective bird hovering over its ward
key_terms.حَافَ: He was unjust, deviated from justice; from the root ح-و-ف indicating deviation and oppression
key_terms.وَكَلَهُ إِلَى نَفْسِهِ: Leaves him to himself — withdrawal of divine support and assistance
key_terms.يَدُ اللَّهِ: Hand of God — a metaphor for divine presence, support, and grace; not to be understood literally

ai.seo_question: What does Islam teach about divine accountability of rulers?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) describes divine oversight of rulers: God's mercy continuously hovers over those in authority, supporting them. However, when a ruler commits injustice, God withdraws that divine support and leaves the ruler entirely to his own devices. This hadith was transmitted through Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) as a teaching on the theological accountability of political authority, reminding rulers that their power is contingent upon just conduct.
